largestHolders.name: Volkswagen AG (indirectly, via Porsche Holding Stuttgart GmbH)

structure.note: Share capital of €911 million: 455.5 million unlisted ordinary (voting) shares and 455.5 million listed nonvoting preferred shares, each with a €1 theoretical interest in the share capital; preferred shares carry a dividend €0.01 higher than ordinary shares. Volkswagen AG indirectly holds 75.0% minus one of the ordinary shares (via Porsche Holding Stuttgart GmbH) and Porsche Automobil Holding SE 25.0% plus one, both unchanged in 2025. Of the preferred shares, around 75.8% is indirectly held by Volkswagen AG and around 24.2% is free float (December 31, 2025). As a percentage of share capital: Volkswagen AG 75.4%, Porsche SE 12.5%, institutional and private investors 12.1%.

notes: All figures from the Porsche AG Annual and Sustainability Report 2025 (consolidated financial statements, IFRS), fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, on investorrelations.porsche.com. EUR, converted exactly from € millions. LEADER: Oliver Blume was Chairman of the Executive Board (CEO) for all of fiscal 2025 and left the Executive Board by mutual agreement effective midnight December 31, 2025, to focus on Volkswagen AG; Dr. Michael Leiters became CEO on January 1, 2026 (Half-Year Financial Report 2026). Relation is therefore former-ceo. The report does not disclose Blume's personal holding of Porsche AG shares (no shareholding table), so status is 'not-disclosed'. HOLDERS: percentages are of total share capital (ordinary plus preferred), as the chart states, so they are economic; Volkswagen's 75.4% and Porsche SE's 12.5% are separate holdings and do not overlap. The report states the structure of investments was unchanged from 2024. No other individual preferred-share holder is disclosed. DIVIDENDS: €2,100 million paid to Porsche AG shareholders in 2025 (statement of changes in equity); the cash-flow line 'Dividends' of €2,101 million includes €1 million to non-controlling interests. BUYBACKS: 0; the cash-flow statement has no line for purchases of own shares and the share count stayed at 455,500,000 of each class. STOCK COMP: null. Share-based payment (note 43) is cash-settled performance share plans for the Executive Board and management, plus an IPO bonus whose final tranche was paid in 2025; no shares are granted. The note gives the expense in parts (Executive Board and top management: total expense of –€5 million; other management: €20 million; IPO bonus: 0) without a company-wide total, so no figure is recorded rather than summing. GEOGRAPHY: the five regions as reported; the 'Hedges sales revenue' column of €232 million is omitted, so the segments sum to €36,039 million against the Group total of €36,272 million.

taxes.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. Taxes: income taxes paid in operating cash flow (€317m).

paidout.notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (Annual and Sustainability Report 2025, IFRS). Interest paid, interest received, dividends received and income taxes paid all sit in operating activities, so nothing is added. Captive-finance growth (leased assets, FS receivables) is inside OCF, as at Volkswagen, so paidOut is inflated by 2,534 € million. Lease principal (135) in financing noted, not added. OCF fell to 3,614 € million from 6,353 largely because profit before tax dropped to 445 € million after the product-strategy realignment charges (depreciation, amortization and impairment of 5,451 € million is added back).

classes.pricedAsReason: The ordinary shares are not listed (Annual and Sustainability Report 2025: '455.5 million are unlisted ordinary shares and 455.5 million are listed nonvoting preferred shares') and are all held by Volkswagen AG and Porsche SE, so they are priced through the preferred line; the two classes have the same €1 interest in share capital and differ only by voting rights and a €0.01 higher dividend on the preferred share. They do not convert.

marketcap.notes: Both classes are counted. Porsche's preferred shares (Vorzugsaktien) are not fixed-claim preferred stock: they share in profits like ordinary shares, carry 'the right to an additional dividend that is €0.01 higher than the ordinary shares, but are non-voting' (Half-Year Financial Report 2026), and each class is half of the €911 million share capital, so the brief's rule to leave out preferred stock is read as not applying. The preferred shares trade on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (Xetra symbol P911, Yahoo P911.DE, EUR); there is no ADR. Pricing the controlling ordinary block at the nonvoting preferred price is a judgment call: no market price exists for it. The count is from the latest report with a share count, the Half-Year Financial Report 2026 (June 30, 2026); the Q3 2026 quarterly statement gives none, and the count has been 455,500,000 of each class since the 2022 IPO, with no treasury shares.

pay.notes: Employees: Porsche AG Group head count at December 31, 2025 (41,780, down from 42,615). The average for 2025 was 42,066, including 741 trainees and 1,010 employees in the release phase of partial retirement (note 42). Payroll: note 41 total personnel expenses of €5,054m (wages and salaries 4,232, social security contributions 631, pension and other benefit costs 191), in billions of EUR. This is the IFRS group figure; the €2,743m 'personnel expenses' in the management report is the parent company Porsche AG alone under HGB and is not used.
